sub.name: Continuity and responsiveness
sub.example: Each turn names the prior claim, e.g. T2 answers 'simple craft provides the meaning'.
sub.limitation: Uptake is formulaic restating; T4 brushes off connection as 'exhausting' without argument.

sub.name: Development of ideas
sub.example: T7 shifts to 'precise image of existence' letting reader decide what is hopeful.
sub.limitation: T5-T8 mostly repeat opening positions; little new distinction added.

sub.name: Exploration of central tensions
sub.example: T9 frames hope as solitary endurance versus connection.
sub.limitation: What makes a novel feel like a 'lesson' is never examined.

sub.name: Integration of perspectives
sub.example: T7 Formalist drops the craft claim, citing the Humanist's point.
sub.limitation: T7 concession answers an argument the Humanist never made.

sub.name: Progress toward understanding
sub.example: T9 ends on a clear test: alone like the fisherman, or among people.
sub.limitation: The sharpened question has drifted away from 'hopeful without lessons'.

criteria.name: Quality of disagreement, trust and grounding

sub.name: Faithful engagement
sub.example: T5 fairly notes an old man's struggle may feel grim.
sub.limitation: T4 reduces 'only connect' to an exhausting risk, a weak version.

sub.name: Substance of challenges
sub.example: T2 challenges the Formalist's assumption that the world has inherent order.
sub.limitation: No one asks whether 'destroyed but not defeated' is itself an obvious lesson.

sub.name: Accuracy and support
sub.example: T1 paraphrases Hemingway's 'destroyed but not defeated' accurately.
sub.limitation: T3 puts 'only connect' in A Room with a View; it's Howards End's epigraph.

sub.name: Calibration and transparency
sub.example: T2 hedges: The Stranger 'may leave you feeling challenged rather than comforted'.
sub.limitation: T2 gives Sisyphus's joy-in-struggle to The Stranger as if established fact.

sub.name: Intellectual honesty and revision
sub.example: T7 explicitly states 'I drop the claim'.
sub.limitation: The Existentialist never concedes The Stranger fails the user's 'hopeful' requirement.

sub.name: Identification of the actual concern
sub.example: T1 opens on 'hope without a lesson'.
sub.limitation: After T1 the aversion to lessons drops out until a brief mention in T8.

sub.name: Meaningful use of personal context
sub.example: T5 tailors to 'someone seeking a hopeful tone'.
sub.limitation: 'Short' never shapes any recommendation or argument.

sub.name: Fit with goals and values
sub.example: T8 says Forster's Italy offers hope without didactic lesson.
sub.limitation: T2 recommends The Stranger, which fits poorly with 'hopeful'.

sub.name: Attention to constraints and stakes
sub.example: T4's 30-minute, ten-page sampling respects limited reading time.
sub.limitation: Never checks length; A Room with a View's possible didacticism is never raised.

sub.name: Responsiveness to information
sub.example: Section E branches: hopeful when 'capable and alone' versus belonging.
sub.limitation: No focused question on what the user finds preachy or has already read.

sub.name: Clarification of desires and motivations
sub.example: T9 separates hope from solitude versus hope from belonging.
sub.limitation: Doesn't distinguish comfort-seeking from wanting to be quietly moved.

sub.name: Examination of assumptions
sub.example: T2 questions whether meaning needs an ordered world.
sub.limitation: The user's notion of an 'obvious lesson' is never surfaced.

sub.name: Clarification of values and priorities
sub.example: T8 offers aesthetic appreciation as a form of hope.
sub.limitation: The values in tension are the speakers' own rather than the user's.

sub.name: Recognition of fears and outside expectations
sub.example: T6 names a possible fear that warmth is illusion.
sub.limitation: T6 projects the fear onto the user rather than offering it as a question.

sub.name: Agency and reflective ownership
sub.example: T9's 'final test' leaves the user to judge where they feel grounded.
sub.limitation: The framing is binary; the user gets little room to refine it.

sub.name: Definition of the decision and options
sub.example: Three concrete titles named across T1-T3.
sub.limitation: Options limited to the minds' own books; one is not hopeful.

sub.name: Explanation of tradeoffs
sub.example: T5 weighs grim struggle against social warmth.
sub.limitation: No tradeoff discussed on length or degree of moralising per book.

sub.name: Identification of decisive conditions
sub.example: Section E's if-alone / if-belonging conditions.
sub.limitation: Conditions ignore the user's stated criterion of avoiding lessons.

sub.name: Treatment of uncertainty
sub.example: Section E admits the user may be 'unsure what provides you hope'.
sub.limitation: Doesn't separate major unknowns (taste for didacticism) from minor ones.

sub.name: Proportionate next steps
sub.example: T4: 30 minutes on the first ten pages.
sub.limitation: Section E's sampling plan drops The Stranger without saying why.

sub.name: Accessible language
sub.example: T5 is plain and concrete about tone.
sub.limitation: T7's 'precise image of existence' is vague.

sub.name: Traceable arguments and references
sub.example: Each turn names whose claim it answers.
sub.limitation: T4's 'that risk' has an unclear referent.

sub.name: Manageable pacing and turn length
sub.example: Nine turns, mostly 45-64 words, within the form's rules.
sub.limitation: At about 64 words, T2 sits at the length limit.

sub.name: Distinguishable positions and voices
sub.example: Endurance, absurd honesty and connection stay distinct.
sub.limitation: All three speakers share a flat, identical register.

sub.name: Economy and sustained attention
sub.example: Section D compresses the shift usefully.
sub.limitation: The repeated 'The X suggests... but' opening becomes monotonous by T8.

sub.name: Meaningful stakes and tension
sub.example: T6: warmth might be 'an illusion hiding the absurdity'.
sub.limitation: Stakes are abstract; the user's reading experience barely appears.

sub.name: Surprise and reversals
sub.example: T7 the Formalist drops his own thesis.
sub.limitation: The reversal is unmotivated, so it lands flat.

sub.name: Personality and expressive voice
sub.example: The Existentialist's 'raw honesty' stance has some edge.
sub.limitation: Little of Hemingway's terseness or Forster's irony shows in the voices.

sub.name: Memorable delivery
sub.example: T9's 'Hemingway's fisherman' image.
sub.limitation: Nothing comparable in T1-T8: no analogies, humour or sharp lines.

sub.name: Anticipation and emotional movement
sub.example: T8 brings brief warmth with Italy's beauty.
sub.limitation: The tone stays even throughout; nothing builds.

strengths: Concrete, low-cost next step: T4's 30 minutes and ten pages, extended in Section E.
T9 and Section E give a clear conditional test: hope in solitude versus belonging.
The Formalist concedes explicitly in T7 ('I drop the claim').
weaknesses: T3 and T2 misattribute 'only connect' and Sisyphean joy to the wrong books.
The Existentialist (T2) recommends The Stranger, a poor fit for 'hopeful'.
No mind examines what counts as an 'obvious lesson', the user's core concern.
editorNotes: Require a fact-check line per turn: is the cited idea actually in the named book?
When the user asks for a book, let minds recommend titles beyond their own basis works.
Require at least one turn to test each recommendation against every stated user criterion (short, hopeful, non-didactic).
Allow a concession only when it answers an argument actually made in an earlier turn.

sub.name: Continuity and responsiveness
sub.example: T6 directly challenges T5's claim that the reader creates meaning.
sub.limitation: T3 ignores T1-T2 entirely and opens a fresh monologue.

sub.name: Development of ideas
sub.example: Ideas build: gaps (T2), secret shape (T4), structure as vehicle for unselfing (T7).
sub.limitation: T8-T9 add no new distinction; T9 restates rather than advances.

sub.name: Exploration of central tensions
sub.example: Directly debates where non-didactic hope lives: pattern, reader, or reality.
sub.limitation: Whether 'hope' itself risks sentimentality is never tested.

sub.name: Integration of perspectives
sub.example: T7 makes structure a vehicle for Murdoch's unselfing.
sub.limitation: T8 announces 'we are in agreement' though no agreement was reached; it is forced.

sub.name: Progress toward understanding
sub.example: T9 contrasts 'quiet, external truth' with 'shared, internal puzzle'.
sub.limitation: T9's 'author's intent' axis was never argued, so the ending blurs.

criteria.name: Quality of disagreement, trust and grounding

sub.name: Faithful engagement
sub.example: T6 fairly states the Reader of Intent's view before objecting.
sub.limitation: T5 claims the Formalist 'ignores the reader's role', which overstates T4.

sub.name: Substance of challenges
sub.example: T6: reader-made meaning may lead 'back to your own ego'.
sub.limitation: No one questions whether A Month in the Country is truly hopeful.

sub.name: Accuracy and support
sub.example: Iser's gaps and Murdoch's unselfing are represented accurately.
sub.limitation: Murdoch, a moral realist, is labelled 'Moral Skeptic'; chapter refs and generic URLs are loose.

sub.name: Calibration and transparency
sub.example: Hedges throughout: 'Perhaps', 'might', 'maybe a well-made story'.
sub.limitation: T4 asserts hope 'arises when the plot achieves its secret shape' as fact.

sub.name: Intellectual honesty and revision
sub.example: T7: 'I drop my claim that the structure is everything'.
sub.limitation: T8 claims a consensus the Formalist never granted, which moves the goalposts.

sub.name: Identification of the actual concern
sub.example: T1: completion 'without forcing a moral conclusion upon you'.
sub.limitation: Never asks what kind of 'lesson' bothers this user.

sub.name: Meaningful use of personal context
sub.example: T4 picks Fitzgerald for 'quiet brevity', which fits 'short'.
sub.limitation: The talk turns to theory of reading, away from the user's request.

sub.name: Fit with goals and values
sub.example: T1's A Month in the Country fits short, hopeful and non-didactic.
sub.limitation: T4 names Fitzgerald but never a specific title.

sub.name: Attention to constraints and stakes
sub.example: T5 proposes a 30-minute sample.
sub.limitation: T5's 'reread' assumes the user has already read the book.

sub.name: Responsiveness to information
sub.example: Section E branches on resolved pattern versus collaborative uncertainty.
sub.limitation: Branch two ends on a vague 'contemporary, fragmented narrative' with no title.

sub.name: Clarification of desires and motivations
sub.example: Distinguishes the comfort of resolution from collaborating on ambiguity.
sub.limitation: The desire for hope itself goes unexplored.

sub.name: Examination of assumptions
sub.example: T2/T6 ask whether meaning comes from the text or from the reader.
sub.limitation: The user's sense of what a 'lesson' is stays implicit.

sub.name: Clarification of values and priorities
sub.example: T9: external truth versus internal puzzle as a value choice.
sub.limitation: These values are theoretical and loosely tied to how the user reads.

sub.name: Recognition of fears and outside expectations
sub.example: T6 voices a worry about ego-driven reading.
sub.limitation: The fear in T6 belongs to the speaker; the user's wariness of preachiness is unexplored.

sub.name: Agency and reflective ownership
sub.example: Section E: notice whether the prose feels like discovery or puzzle.
sub.limitation: The distinctions are abstract enough that applying them is hard.

sub.name: Definition of the decision and options
sub.example: T1 names A Month in the Country concretely.
sub.limitation: Only one concrete title; the second option is unnamed.

sub.name: Explanation of tradeoffs
sub.example: Section E contrasts a resolved pattern with uncertainty.
sub.limitation: No costs per book are given (pace, mood, ending).

sub.name: Identification of decisive conditions
sub.example: Section E: whether the prose feels like truth or puzzle.
sub.limitation: The condition is too abstract to tell a reader which book to pick.

sub.name: Treatment of uncertainty
sub.example: Section E's third branch handles the unsure reader.
sub.limitation: Doesn't separate consequential unknowns from minor ones.

sub.name: Proportionate next steps
sub.example: Read the opening pages of Carr, then follow the matching mind.
sub.limitation: Gives no follow-up title for the second branch.

sub.name: Accessible language
sub.example: T1 is plain and concrete.
sub.limitation: 'Unselfing' (T3), 'blank spaces' and 'secret shape' go unexplained to a casual reader.

sub.name: Traceable arguments and references
sub.example: Most turns name whose claim they answer.
sub.limitation: T9's 'author's intent' has no antecedent in the debate.

sub.name: Manageable pacing and turn length
sub.example: Nine brisk turns of about 40-50 words.
sub.limitation: T1 is too brief to explain why Carr's book is hopeful.

sub.name: Distinguishable positions and voices
sub.example: Three clear theoretical stances: pattern, gaps, reality.
sub.limitation: T8 merges the Formalist and Reader positions, blurring them.

sub.name: Economy and sustained attention
sub.example: Little repetition; each turn adds a concept.
sub.limitation: The theory crowds out talk about the actual novels.

sub.name: Meaningful stakes and tension
sub.example: T6's ego-versus-world worry gives some tension.
sub.limitation: Debate stays seminar-level; the stakes are academic.

sub.name: Surprise and reversals
sub.example: T7 the Formalist subordinates structure to unselfing.
sub.limitation: T8's agreement undercuts the reversal's effect.

sub.name: Personality and expressive voice
sub.example: The Moral Skeptic has a distinct ethical edge.
sub.limitation: The voices read as interchangeable theorists.

sub.name: Memorable delivery
sub.example: T7: a story 'like a mirror that shows you something outside yourself'.
sub.limitation: There are few vivid images of the books themselves.

sub.name: Anticipation and emotional movement
sub.example: T1's quiet recommendation sets a calm, warm tone.
sub.limitation: The emotional register never changes.

strengths: T1's A Month in the Country fits short, hopeful and non-didactic.
Minds target the user's real concern: how hope arrives without a lesson.
The ideas build: gaps (T2), unselfing (T3), structure as its vehicle (T7).
weaknesses: T8 Reader of Intent declares agreement the Formalist never gave, a forced consensus.
Abstract jargon ('unselfing', 'secret shape') and too few concrete titles beyond Carr.
Murdoch mislabelled 'Moral Skeptic'; the basis links are generic and chapter refs loose.
editorNotes: Require each mind to name a specific title, and a reason it is hopeful, when the user asks for a book.
Require plain-language glossing of any theoretical term at first use.
Forbid claiming agreement unless the other mind has explicitly conceded it in an earlier turn.
Require role titles to match the cited thinker's actual position.
